local_metric_computation.method: AST: any def whose NAME matches a metric (sharpe|ic|fitness|turnover|drawdown|pnl|ret) AND whose body computes one (.corr/.mean()/.std()/sqrt(252)/annualiz/cumprod). Zeros re-verified by grep for .corr(|spearman|pearson|sqrt(252)|annualiz|cumprod outside tests.

verdicts.s16_prior_correction: But the 13 zeros are largely VACUOUS. 10 of 13 authorships compute NO factor metric locally at all -- every "sharpe" in them is .get() off the platform simulation response or a hardcoded literal. A repo with no evaluation stage cannot carry a multiplicity control, so its zero is not evidence of an oversight. The non-vacuous statement is: of the 3 authorships that compute a factor score themselves, 0 carry any multiplicity control. n=3, not 13.
verdicts.where_the_exposure_actually_lives: The class outsources statistics AND out-of-sample to WorldQuant own simulator. Its multiplicity exposure is therefore not in its code vocabulary at all -- it is the COUNT OF SIMULATIONS FIRED, which s16 already measured as gen_scale_hits and did not connect. Any future measurement of this class multiplicity must be a generation-scale measurement, not a grep.
